Assumptions and isolation: compare the same checkpoint, tokenizer, runtime and serving versions, decoding limits, request trace and output-length distribution, scheduler, batching policy, hardware/topology, drivers, power, and thermal envelope. Change only weight precision; hold activation and KV-cache precision, prompt set, calibration procedure, and unrelated optimization passes fixed. Record bit width, group size, scale/zero-point and outlier policy, calibration provenance, held-out split, selected kernels, and fallback routes. Use an authorized disposable environment and redact telemetry.

Falsifiable hypothesis for scenario variant 199: at each predeclared concurrency, weight-only quantization reduces fully loaded cost per successful output token by a predeclared target while held-out quality, safety, correctness, TTFT, and TPOT remain within predeclared gates. Keep calibration and held-out sets disjoint. Confounders include thermal throttling, cache state, scheduler interference, compilation, prompt/output mix, retries, and unsupported kernels silently invoking higher-precision paths; log and stratify these, and rerun or invalidate trials when isolation fails. Gate a bounded authorized canary on the same hard limits, monitor quality, safety, errors, latency, and cost, stop on any breach, and retain an immediate tested rollback to the baseline. Evidence must include versioned configs, kernel/fallback logs, calibration and held-out provenance, trial assignments, confidence intervals, failure/cleanup records, authorization, and rollback results.
